stories.headline: House Faces Vote on Impeaching Hegseth Over Iran War
stories.dek: Rep. Thomas Massie forced a floor vote on eight articles against the Defense Secretary, with a motion to table expected first.
pole_a_bullets: Impeachment is meant for misconduct, not for disagreement over a war the commander in chief ordered.
Hegseth calls the effort a farce and a stunt aimed at hurting President Trump.
Massie is the lone Republican seeking removal, and defenders say Hegseth has been effective.
A lame-duck session already faces a government funding deadline and judicial confirmations. Leaders call the push a distraction.
pole_b_bullets: The Iran war was waged without a declaration of war or statutory authorization, and war powers belong to Congress.
Minority Leader Jeffries is a hard yes and calls Hegseth the architect of a reckless, failed war.
The articles also cite the seizure of Venezuela's president and killings of alleged drug smugglers, which they present as a pattern of abuse.
Voters just handed Republicans a wipeout, and many in the GOP blame the war. Supporters say accountability should not wait.
stories.pole_a_who: Positions commonly voiced by Hegseth, Speaker Mike Johnson and House GOP leaders.
stories.pole_b_who: Positions commonly voiced by House Democratic leaders, Rep. Massie and war-powers advocates.
evidence_left: <cite index="104-1,104-3">Massie reintroduced articles of impeachment on Monday. They include eight charges, largely related to the Iran war.</cite> <cite index="104-6,104-7">Because the measure is privileged, GOP leaders must schedule a vote within two legislative days. A simple majority is needed to approve the articles.</cite>

<cite index="105-3">CBS News reported the House is expected to take up the resolution Tuesday evening, likely after a procedural vote to table it.</cite> The outcome was not known at the time of writing.
evidence_right: <cite index="12-3">Hegseth called the effort a farce and a stunt at a Pentagon news conference Tuesday morning.</cite>

<cite index="102-1">The Hill reports that, despite some GOP criticism of Hegseth, Massie has been the lone Republican calling for his removal.</cite> <cite index="105-7">Jeffries said Monday he is a hard yes.</cite>
stories.sources_line: Sourced from CBS News, NBC News, The Hill, November 10, 2026.

stories.headline: Hot October CPI Puts Half-Point Fed Hike on the Table
stories.dek: Core prices rose 0.3% against a 0.2% forecast, and stocks fell a day after their best session since April.
pole_a_bullets: Headline CPI slowed to 0.4% from 0.6% in September as the gasoline surge faded.
October payrolls rose 165,000 against a 65,000 forecast, and unemployment fell to 4.1%. The Fed can tighten without breaking the labor market.
Brent crude dropped below $90, which should ease energy-driven inflation.
Monday's rally showed dip-buyers are still willing to back AI and tech stocks. A quarter-point hike is already priced in.
pole_b_bullets: Core CPI has risen 0.3% for three straight months, so inflation is broadening beyond energy.
Waller says a 25-point hike alone would risk the Fed's credibility, and a 50-point move is now live.
Inflation is wiping out wage gains, and midterm voters already punished incumbents over prices.
Two-year yields jumped and stocks reversed, a sign that more tightening is hitting valuations.
stories.pole_a_who: Positions commonly voiced by bullish strategists and investors citing labor-market strength and falling oil.
stories.pole_b_who: Positions commonly voiced by inflation-focused economists and hawkish Fed officials such as Gov. Waller.
evidence_left: <cite index="83-2,83-3">The BLS reported CPI up a seasonally adjusted 0.4% in October. Core CPI rose 0.3%.</cite> <cite index="83-5,83-6">Economists surveyed by Dow Jones expected 0.3% headline and 0.2% core.</cite>
<cite index="32-4,32-5">October employers added 165,000 jobs against a Reuters-polled forecast of 65,000. Unemployment fell to 4.1% from 4.2%.</cite>
evidence_right: <cite index="84-1">Fed Governor Waller said a core reading of 0.3% would prompt him to consider a half-point hike at the Dec. 8-9 meeting.</cite> The 50-basis-point odds differ by source: <cite index="83-9">13.6% per CNBC, citing CME FedWatch</cite>, <cite index="86-1">15% per Reuters</cite> and <cite index="88-5">nearly 11% per Investing.com</cite>.

<cite index="19-6,19-9">Stocks fell Tuesday, one day after the S&P 500 posted its best day since April.</cite> <cite index="87-9">The two-year Treasury yield rose 0.13 percentage point, per Axios.</cite>
stories.sources_line: Sourced from CNBC, Reuters via Investing.com, Axios, 24/7 Wall St., November 10, 2026.

stories.headline: Nvidia Board Opens Probe After CEO Admits Affair With Alleged Chinese Spy
stories.dek: Jensen Huang admitted the relationship in a staff memo, and lawmakers are scrutinizing Nvidia's Megaspeed ties.
pole_a_bullets: The board says it has no reason to believe national security or company secrets were compromised and has confidence in Huang.
Nvidia says Megaspeed is a cloud service permitted under export-control rules.
Nvidia's leadership in AI chips is a strategic US asset, so a distraction-driven shake-up could hand ground to China.
Some analysts call Huang not replaceable and rate the chance of his removal as small.
pole_b_bullets: US intelligence reportedly believes China's MSS recruited Alice Huang to target the CEO, which makes this a counterintelligence matter, not only a personal one.
Nvidia first described the contacts as ordinary customer dealings. Critics say the board should test earlier statements by the CEO and company.
The board announced its probe 10 days after the first report and pre-announced confidence in Huang. Critics doubt its independence.
Democrats and Republicans want answers on chip smuggling and on what the administration knew.
stories.pole_a_who: Positions commonly voiced by Nvidia's board, company defenders and some Wall Street analysts.
stories.pole_b_who: Positions commonly voiced by members of Congress in both parties, export-control hawks and governance critics.
evidence_left: <cite index="75-5,75-7">Nvidia's board said Sunday it is opening an independent investigation. A committee of independent directors, assisted by outside counsel, will oversee it.</cite>
<cite index="75-3,75-9">Huang acknowledged being unfaithful in an employee memo. The board said it has no reason to believe national security or Nvidia secrets were compromised.</cite>
evidence_right: <cite index="76-4">The New York Times and Financial Times reported that US intelligence agencies worry Alice Huang, tied to customer Megaspeed, has been passing information to Beijing.</cite> <cite index="77-1">CNBC describes the intelligence assessment as reported, not officially released.</cite>

<cite index="77-9">Lawmakers are calling for an investigation and questioning what the Trump administration knew.</cite> The New York Times also reported a Commerce probe of Megaspeed moved to the Justice Department. That claim was relayed via a newsletter and not independently confirmed here.
stories.sources_line: Sourced from NBC News, CNBC, Fast Company, November 10, 2026.

stories.headline: Anthropic Sets IPO Terms Targeting Up to $1.4 Trillion Valuation
stories.dek: The Claude maker seeks up to $64.4 billion, well below the $2 trillion once discussed.
pole_a_bullets: A listing of this size would fund expansion in a fierce race with OpenAI.
Cornerstone investors including Google, Nvidia and AMD are backing a separate $26 billion placement.
Going public ahead of OpenAI makes Anthropic the first frontier AI lab on the market and sets the benchmark for the sector.
Even a $1 trillion-plus valuation is remarkable and marks a rise from the $965 billion last private round.
pole_b_bullets: The valuation fell from the $2 trillion once discussed, a sign of cooling appetite for AI.
Roughly $900 billion in compute commitments to partners like Amazon and Google weigh on the business.
Growth has slowed this year, and some investors questioned whether the $1.5 trillion talk was too high.
Volatility in AI stocks, including Nvidia's slide, makes timing and pricing riskier.
stories.pole_a_who: Positions commonly voiced by AI-sector bulls, IPO underwriters and growth investors.
stories.pole_b_who: Positions commonly voiced by valuation skeptics, credit analysts and AI-bubble critics.
evidence_left: <cite index="94-4">The IPO would sell 825 million shares in an indicative band of $70 to $78, raising up to $64.4 billion.</cite> <cite index="94-7">A separate $26 billion private placement involves Google, Nvidia and AMD.</cite>

Reported valuations differ by outlet. <cite index="94-3">NBC News cited up to $1.02 trillion</cite>, <cite index="96-1">the AP about $1.3 trillion</cite> and <cite index="97-3">Bloomberg about $1.4 trillion</cite>. <cite index="92-5">TheWrap said the roughly $1 trillion figure uses outstanding shares and the higher one adds options.</cite>
evidence_right: <cite index="94-1,94-2">Investors once expected an October IPO at up to $2 trillion. Tuesday's filing points to about half that.</cite>
<cite index="92-7">Reuters, via TheWrap, reported nearly $900 billion in computing commitments.</cite> <cite index="95-12">Fast Company reported that Anthropic's growth has slowed this year.</cite>
stories.sources_line: Sourced from NBC News, Bloomberg, AP via U.S. News, TheWrap, November 10, 2026.

stories.headline: Supreme Court Lets Big Bend Border Wall Construction Resume
stories.dek: An unsigned 8-1 order pauses a district judge's ruling while the administration seeks full review.
pole_a_bullets: Federal law lets the Homeland Security Secretary waive laws to speed barrier construction, and the lower order blocked that authority.
The statute limits judges' power to intervene when the government finds swift construction necessary.
The Court found the government's interest outweighs the aesthetic, recreational and environmental harms alleged.
An 8-1 order, with most justices joining, suggests the legal question is not close.
pole_b_bullets: The district judge found Congress likely did not authorize waivers this broad.
Building through a national park risks lasting damage to the landscape that a later ruling cannot undo.
Justice Jackson dissented, and critics say emergency orders skip full review of a major environmental question.
Opponents say sweeping waivers let the executive sidestep environmental laws Congress wrote.
stories.pole_a_who: Positions commonly voiced by the Trump administration, border-security advocates and conservative outlets.
stories.pole_b_who: Positions commonly voiced by environmental groups, Big Bend-area opponents and Justice Jackson's dissent.
evidence_left: <cite index="67-5">In an unsigned 8-1 ruling, the justices put U.S. District Judge Kathleen Cardone's order on hold, allowing construction to resume while the administration seeks review.</cite>

<cite index="68-8,68-9">The Daily Signal reports the Court agreed that federal law limits judges' power to intervene. It quoted the Court saying the lower order bars the Secretary from exercising his statutory waiver authority.</cite>
evidence_right: <cite index="67-3,67-7">Justice Jackson dissented. The ruling is temporary until the Court decides whether to hear the case or the lower court in El Paso settles it.</cite>
<cite index="68-6,68-7">The project was to include 30-foot-tall steel barriers in some areas. The district court had found Congress likely did not authorize the broad waivers.</cite>
stories.sources_line: Sourced from KFOX (Texas), The Daily Signal, SCOTUSblog, November 10, 2026.

stories.headline: Jaguars Go All In With Three Trades Before the Deadline
stories.dek: Jacksonville (6-2) added Jessie Bates, Davon Godchaux and Jordan Davis, giving up a 2027 first-round pick.
pole_a_bullets: The Jaguars lead the AFC South with top-five scoring offense and defense, so adding three defenders fits a real contender.
Davis, 26, is a proven interior force, and Bates adds a Pro Bowl safety.
ESPN's Seth Walder-style bold take is that Jacksonville wins the AFC, and early odds put them among Super Bowl favorites.
Draft picks matter less than a Super Bowl window in a top-heavy league.
pole_b_bullets: Giving up a 2027 first and second plus a 2029 second for one lineman is a steep price. SI called it a risky bet.
ESPN's grade for the deal reportedly called it a disaster for Jacksonville. The Eagles, at 2-7, got the better end.
Davis just signed a $78 million extension, which adds to the cost of a defensive tackle who played 52% of snaps in Philadelphia.
Many contenders crowd the top tier, so the extra defense may not separate Jacksonville from the pack.
stories.pole_a_who: Positions commonly voiced by Jaguars fans and some NFL analysts.
stories.pole_b_who: Positions commonly voiced by trade-grade critics and Eagles-side analysts.
evidence_left: <cite index="116-3,116-4">On Monday the Jaguars acquired safety Jessie Bates III from Atlanta, tackle Davon Godchaux from New Orleans and tackle Jordan Davis from Philadelphia. Davis cost a 2027 first-round pick and a 2029 second-round pick.</cite>
<cite index="52-5">Yahoo Sports lists the Jaguars as 10.5-point road favorites against the Titans in Week 10.</cite>
evidence_right: <cite index="113-10">Jacksonville no longer has a 2027 first- or second-round pick after Monday's deals.</cite> <cite index="112-11">The NY Post reports the Eagles stand at 2-7 after seven straight losses.</cite>

<cite index="113-8">Davis signed a three-year, $78 million extension with the Eagles in March.</cite> <cite index="119-9">The Philadelphia Inquirer reports ESPN's assessment of the deal was sharply negative for Jacksonville.</cite>
stories.sources_line: Sourced from CBS Sports, Yahoo Sports, Sports Illustrated, The Philadelphia Inquirer, November 10, 2026.
